epic.name: Hazine Preview Delivery
decisions: The controller must verify Phase 0 created a clean dedicated canonical baseline branch/commit before launching this epic.
Run Spectrum from C:/Users/digit/GriotClients/Hazine, never from the non-Git working snapshot.
This is an honest progress build; its validation report must distinguish present, provisional, and deferred behavior.
Use direct three-globe and keep approved brand assets and original GLBs immutable.
Resolve the actual remote and Pages target without guessing.

Before changing R3F or runtime asset-loading behavior, read C:/Users/digit/.agents/skills/griot-r3f/SKILL.md and the task-relevant loading/performance recipes; treat them as implementation requirements.
risks: Root-absolute assets fail below the repository base
SPA fallback drops the base prefix
A guessed remote publishes to the wrong repository
A preview can overstate unfinished behavior

stories.title: Resolve assets beneath the repository base
stories.description: As a preview visitor, every runtime model, texture, brand, and navigation asset loads beneath the configured GitHub Pages repository base.

steps.description: Create assetUrl(path) around import.meta.env.BASE_URL.
Migrate model, texture, brand, and navigation references.
Build with a simulated repository base and inspect emitted asset URLs.

context.why: The preview must load when Pages serves it below a repository prefix.
risks: Mixed absolute and base-aware paths create partial scene failures.
edgeCases: Leading slashes, root local development, and already-prefixed paths.
patterns: Centralize all runtime URL construction in src/lib/assetUrl.js.

stories.title: Load the workbench directly on Pages
stories.description: As a preview visitor, I can navigate directly to or refresh /workbench beneath the repository base without a 404.

steps.description: Generate dist/workbench/index.html and dist/404.html after build.
Make route selection and fallback restoration base-aware.
Direct-load and refresh /hazine/workbench/ in a production preview.

context.why: The workbench is a first-class shareable preview route.
risks: Fallback restoration can lose query/path state or the base prefix.
patterns: Generate static route entry plus Pages-compatible SPA fallback.

stories.title: Pin the preview dependency set
stories.description: As a maintainer rebuilding the preview, I receive explicit compatible dependency ranges instead of mutable latest releases.

steps.description: Resolve proven versions from the baseline lockfile.
Replace latest specifiers with compatible explicit ranges.
Install from the frozen lockfile and build.

context.why: A shareable proof must rebuild deterministically.
risks: Range changes can alter React/Three peer compatibility.
edgeCases: React 19 compatibility with R3F, Theatre, and direct three-globe.
patterns: Retain direct three-globe and reject r3f-globe.

stories.title: Build the preview reproducibly in Pages CI
stories.description: As a maintainer, the same frozen install and production build create deployable root, workbench, and fallback artifacts locally and in GitHub Pages CI.

steps.description: Create a Pages workflow with frozen install, build, dist upload, and deploy jobs.
Use the same build path locally and in CI.
Assert dist root, workbench entry, 404 fallback, and base-prefixed assets exist.

context.why: Deployment must not rely on unrecorded local state.
risks: CI and local scripts can diverge.
edgeCases: Repository-derived base differs from local simulation.
patterns: One canonical package build script called by CI.

stories.title: Publish an honest preview validation
stories.description: As a reviewer, I can see exactly which Hazine preview behaviors are present, provisional, or deferred, with evidence for the deployed progress scope.

steps.description: Define the preview-only acceptance matrix.
Record build, asset, root/workbench route, console, and responsive evidence.
List full-experience and hardening behaviors as explicitly deferred rather than implied complete.

context.why: A progress build must be shareable without misrepresenting product completeness.
risks: Using final PRD language can overclaim the preview.
edgeCases: A partially working chapter or interaction.
patterns: Use present/provisional/deferred status with concrete evidence links.

stories.title: Configure the exact Hazine remote
stories.description: As a maintainer, the canonical repository points to the explicitly discovered TheDigitalGriot Hazine remote and Pages target rather than an inferred destination.

steps.description: Discover the existing organization repository and Pages configuration from authoritative GitHub state.
Record the resolved repository, remote URL, default branch, and Pages source.
Configure and verify the canonical remote without changing unrelated Git settings.

context.why: No remote is currently configured and guessing could publish client work incorrectly.
risks: Wrong repository, organization, branch, or Pages source.
edgeCases: Repository does not yet exist and requires an explicit external decision.
patterns: Discovery and evidence before Git remote mutation.

stories.title: Deploy the reviewed preview commit
stories.description: As a maintainer, only the reviewed progress commit is pushed and deployed through the configured Pages workflow.

steps.description: Review and commit the preview diff atomically.
Push the configured deployment branch and observe the Pages workflow.
Record the commit SHA and workflow/deployment result.

context.why: The public preview must correspond to an exact reviewed state.
risks: Publishing a dirty or different commit invalidates the proof.
edgeCases: Workflow succeeds for a superseded commit.
patterns: Commit-based deployment with SHA equality checks.

stories.title: Verify public preview routes
stories.description: As a preview visitor, the public root and direct /workbench URL load the reviewed commit with assets, refresh behavior, console, and desktop/mobile layout intact.

steps.description: Confirm public deployment SHA equals the reviewed preview commit.
Exercise root and direct/refresh workbench flows with console and network capture.
Verify both routes on desktop and mobile and record the live URLs.

context.why: CI success does not prove public routing, assets, or runtime behavior.
risks: Cached older deploys and Pages subpath 404s.
edgeCases: Hard refresh, trailing slash, and mobile safe areas.
patterns: Verify the public artifact, not only the workflow result.
